key_insight: In a Houston 2024 simulation replay, a county-risk reserve policy increased observed five-hour backup coverage from 75.0% to 86.5% and modeled annualized margin by USD 10.2 per home versus a fixed 20% reserve.
engineering_relevance: Risk-adaptive battery reserves could help residential fleets balance market revenue with household backup service.
method: Release HomeFleet-ERCOT, pairing observed prices and county outages with identified simulated homes and causal controller inputs.
Compare independent-home optimization with 21 proximal policy optimization (PPO) training runs.
Evaluate transfer across time, geography, fleets, and storms, plus synthetic warning failures and battery degradation.
evidence_signal: The paired 95% interval for annualized margin gain was USD +1.7 to +21.7 per home, while the coverage-gain interval included zero; only 19.5% of 41 county mass-outage episodes provided enough continuous warning for every battery preset.
watch_item: Results are conditional simulations, not measured company reliability; alert-based charging guarantees depend on sufficient warning, energy, and power.
paper_title: Adaptive Reliability Reserves for Residential Battery Fleets
